Missoula property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Missoula

  • Montana Department of Revenue handles assessment.
  • Missoula County Clerk & Recorder/Treasurer bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

Real property taxes due on or before the last day in November and May (next business day if weekend/holiday); mail must be postmarked by due date. Delinquent: 2% penalty plus interest at 10% annualized; tax liens attach first business day in August.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Request informal review with the Montana DOR via Form AB-26 within 30 days of the date on the classification and appraisal notice (late requests accepted until June 1, 2026 for TY2026 only), or appeal directly to the County Tax Appeal Board by filing with the county clerk and recorder within 30 days of the notice date (or within 30 days of the AB-26 determination). CTAB decisions may be appealed to the Montana Tax Appeal Board within 30 days, then district court (60 days). To preserve a refund, . See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Missoula rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Montana structure: the state Department of Revenue appraises/classifies all real property; the county treasurer bills and collects (including city, school and special district levies). Cities do not assess or collect.
  • Appraisal cycle: residential/commercial valued every two years (2025-2026 cycle, valuation date January 1, 2024).
  • Delinquent taxes cannot be protested or appealed (Yellowstone County bill text).

Missoula by the numbers

The Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey counts about 75,600 people in Missoula, which makes it the 2nd largest of the 7 mt places we cover. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $427,400, 20% above the median of those 7 places. 48% of occupied homes are owner-occupied and 52% are rented, against a median of 60% owner-occupancy across the mt places. The median home was built in 1981, about 42 years ago, which matters for roofs, plumbing and inspection requests. These numbers describe Missoula as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
